title: The Reverse Big Push: Generative AI and Self-Fulfilling Automation
abstract: arXiv:2608.25602v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative AI relocates the fixed cost of automation. A model provider pays to train a frontier system, while a downstream firm rents capability by usage; the same firm must carry a continuing payroll to supply a human-augmented service. We study this asymmetry in a local service economy with household budgets and a market-clearing wage. Human augmentation earns a larger surplus from an additional customer, whereas automation has the lower break-even scale. Payroll supports demand across sectors. Wage adjustment works against this feedback but does not generally undo it: when the wage-income effect dominates the fall in the wage bill per retained worker, production modes are strategic complements. The economy can then possess both a high-demand human-augmented equilibrium and a low-demand automated equilibrium. translated_title: 反向大推动：生成式人工智能与自我实现的自动化
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能将自动化的固定成本重新定位。模型提供商付费训练前沿系统，而下游企业按使用量租用能力；同一企业必须持续支付工资以提供人类增强服务。我们在一个具有家庭预算和市场出清工资的地方服务经济中研究这种不对称性。人类增强从额外客户中获取更大盈余，而自动化具有更低的盈亏平衡规模。工资支付支持跨部门需求。工资调整对抗这种反馈，但通常不会完全抵消它：当工资收入效应主导每个保留工人工资账单的下降时，生产方式成为战略互补。经济随后可能同时具有高需求的人类增强均衡和低需求的自动化均衡。前者是局部最优，即使灵活工资阻止企业利润排序。面对前瞻性企业和交错决策，存在多重均衡，自动化可能自我实现。
tldr: 本文发现生成式AI将自动化固定成本转移给模型提供商，而下游企业承担持续工资，导致在工资收入效应主导时，人类增强与自动化形成战略互补，经济可存在多重均衡，自动化可能自我实现，但人类增强是局部最优。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that generative AI shifts automation's fixed costs to model providers while downstream firms bear ongoing payroll, creating strategic complementarity between human augmentation and automation when the wage-income effect dominates, leading to multiple equilibria where automation can be self-fulfilling, yet human augmentation is locally optimal.
